questions.prompt: In Google's docs, what does "deprecation" mean for a model?

options.text: A notice that the model will be shut down.
options.explanation: Right. After shutdown, the model is completely turned off.

options.text: A free upgrade to a better and faster version.
options.explanation: A deprecation is a warning about shutdown, not an upgrade.

options.text: A lower price for older models.
options.explanation: The term is about support ending, not price.

questions.prompt: You need 300 quick draft thumbnails and one 4K hero image. What does Google say about Nano Banana 2 Lite?

options.text: It is fast and cheap, but supports only 1K.
options.explanation: Right. Good for the thumbnails; the 4K hero needs another model.

options.text: It is the best Google model for 4K hero images.
options.explanation: The docs say it only supports 1K resolution.

questions.prompt: OpenAI's docs list a known weak spot for its image models. Which one?

options.text: They can't make landscape images at all, only square and portrait ones.
They may not keep a recurring character the same across images.
options.explanation: Right. Plan a check for consistency across a campaign.

options.text: They only accept prompts under ten words.
options.explanation: The docs say nothing like this. Complex prompts are allowed, but can take up to 2 minutes.
